key_insight: Training and evaluating models with case-grounded inputs — a local case context plus explicit external evidence — reveals and reduces models' tendency to ignore evidence; the paper provides a framework to build supervision that ties decisions directly to supporting evidence.
problem_solved: Addresses weak supervision and loose evidence–claim coupling that allow models to predict correctly without depending on the provided evidence, and the lack of evaluation protocols that directly test evidence dependence.
method: Introduce the case-grounded evidence verification framework: each example supplies a local case context, external evidence, and a target decision so supervision can be tied to evidence presence.
Construct evidence-sensitive supervision via controlled dataset interventions (e.g., perturbations/counterfactuals) that make labels conditional on evidence support.
Design evaluation diagnostics and metrics that measure evidence dependence (not just accuracy), exposing when models ignore or exploit spurious cues.
impact: Provides practitioners with a practical recipe to build datasets and evaluations that force models to use evidence, improving reliability and interpretability in high-stakes domains (e.g., fact-checking, medical decision support).

paper_title: Case-Grounded Evidence Verification: A Framework for Constructing Evidence-Sensitive Supervision
paper_authors: Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh, Mehdi Joodaki, Mahshad Lotfinia, Sven Nebelung, Daniel Truhn
